correctness.rationale: Restricting the two weighted sextics to x0=0 gives w²=(t³−r²)/(t³−1), hence genus-two hyperelliptic y²=(t³−1)(t³−r²). Six distinct branch points imply smooth genus 2. The S3 stabilizer of two rotated triangles has generic reduced order 6; regular hexagon s=−1 gives 12 and octahedral s²+52s+1=0 gives 24. Double lifts produce 12,24,48. The explicit 72-member surface subgroup and six-element diagonal restriction kernel yield image order 12, using published upper bound. Original surface classification identifies r~1/r; curve s~1/s; then u=v²−2. Independent symbolic identity and polynomial checks corroborate. Finite complex stabilizer samples alone do not prove the uniform classification.

value.rationale: A natural canonical-divisor invariant fails to separate distinct surfaces: u=v²−2 is an explicit non-Torelli map, and the exceptional index-two/index-four extension obstructions locate where new curve symmetries are not global surface symmetries. These are geometric structural facts, not an arbitrary parameter calculation.

final_claim: For the 72-automorphism smooth weighted-sextic X_r, its genus-two canonical curve has parameter s=r² up to inversion, with u=v²−2, fixed extension image order 12 kernel Z/6 and curve automorphism jump to 24 and 48 at hexagonal and Bolza loci.
limitations: Only smooth family r≠0,±1 over C, coarse-parameter map not stack ramification; no claim to broader Torelli classification.
